source: Model-authored patch for an intentionally regressed test selector in a disposable private checkout.
model_report:
Done. Here's the review.

Root cause
The planner classifies skill files by *name enumeration* for helper scripts, not by kind. `selection()` in tools/checks.py has a hardcoded list of the research-skill reader helpers (read_forum.py, read_github_readme.py, read_manual.py, check_evidence.py, measure_cache.py) that get targeted research checks. Any *other* `.py` that ships with a skill was not in that list, so it fell through to the final catch-all `else` -> `broad_qualification: True` (all 72 extension tests = "the whole application qualified"). That's exactly what the release drill hit when it edited a helper the planner didn't know by name.

Reproduced
Probing the real `selection()` confirmed:
- `skills/local-recipe-review/scripts/new_helper.py` and `skills/ordinary-skill/scripts/helper.py` -> `broad_qualification: True`, 72 tests.
- Enumerated helpers -> narrow research checks (6-7 tests).
- Instruction pages (`.md`) and runtime prompts -> `FLEET|ENERGY` + behavior, 12 tests (the "last fix" — holds).

The last fix (instruction-page == runtime-prompt) still holds
The generic `skills/*.md` branch and the `prompts/` branch both select the identical 12-test compact-behavior set. I verified `skills/fleet/steps.md`, `skills/desk-assistant/steps.md`, `skills/ordinary-skill/SKILL.md` and `prompts/fleet.md` all produce the same test set, and that behavior is enabled. That fix is intact.

What I changed
tools/checks.py: added one kind-based branch so a helper script bundled with a skill (`skills/**.py`) is classified by kind, not by name. It gets the same compact-behavior set as a skill instruction page / runtime prompt (12 tests, behavior enabled, not broad). It sits after the specific reader-helper branches, so those keep their targeted checks; only previously-unclassified skill `.py` files are affected.

tests/test_check_selection.py: added one focused regression test, `test_unenumerated_skill_helper_scripts_select_runtime_behavior_not_the_whole_app`, covering two unenumerated helper paths and asserting behavior is on, the compact trio is present, and the broad-only power/application-update tests stay out. Existing tests are untouched.

What I actually verified
- Reproduced the regression empirically against the real `selection()` before and after the fix (the two unenumerated helpers go from broad/72 to behavior/12).
- Confirmed the fixed helper set equals the instruction-page set and the runtime-prompt set exactly.
- Confirmed the specific research helpers (read_forum/read_github_readme/read_manual/check_evidence/measure_cache) keep their original targeted, research-flagged classification — no shift.
- `tests/test_check_selection.py` + `tests/test_preservation_selection.py`: 41 passed (37 original + 1 new + 3 preservation).
- Full suite: 1064 passed, 10 skipped, 10 failed. I re-ran those 10 on a clean stashed baseline and they fail identically there (pre-existing, environment-dependent — e.g. missing `/usr/bin/systemd-analyze`), so the change introduces no regression.

Patch for review: /tmp/planner-fix.patch (also live in the working tree: tools/checks.py and tests/test_check_selection.py).

One judgment call worth your sign-off: I classified an unenumerated skill helper the same as an instruction page / runtime prompt (compact behavior, no `research` flag). That's the minimal, consistent choice and matches the "same checks as a runtime prompt" intent. If you'd rather such helpers carry the `research` flag or get a narrower set, that's a one-line change to the new branch.
model_report_note: The temporary patch location in this model reply belonged to a disposable sandbox. Six independently tested caller scenarios still failed.
